, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

The claimant is in appeal seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT-V, Vijayapur (for short 'Tribunal) in MVC No.140/2021, vide judgment and award dated 25.11.2021.
2.

The claimants are the parents of the deceased Muttaraj, aged 6 years, who was killed in a road traffic accident on 09.07.2020, when a bus belonging to Karnataka State Road Transportation Corporation (henceforth referred as 'Corporation') dashed against him.

The claimants therefore filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'M.V.Act, 1988')
claiming compensation from the Corporation.

3. The claim petition was resisted by the Corporation, who contended that the deceased was NC:
2023:KHC-K:1365 negligent and was responsible for his death and that its driver was not rash or negligent in driving the bus.
4. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant No.2 was examined as PW.1 and Exs.P1 to P7 were marked.
The Corporation examined its driver as RW.1 but did not furnish any documentary evidence.

5. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident was due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the bus belonging to the Corporation and that the deceased died in the accident.

In so far as quantum of compensation is concerned, the Tribunal considered the claim in the light of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Kishan Gopal and Another vs.
Lala and Others reported in (2014) 1 SCC 244 and considered the annual notional income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.30,000/- per annum and applied the multiplier as prescribed in the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of SARLA VERMA (SMT) & OTHERS NC:
2023:KHC-K:1365 VS. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION & ANOTHER, reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 and awarded a sum of Rs.4,80,000/- and a sum of Rs.50,000/- under the conventional heads.

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and award, the claimants are in appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.

7. The learned counsel for the appellants/claimants contended that the Apex Court in the case of Kishan Gopal (supra) departed from the until then conservative method of assessing the compensation and factored the rate of inflation and the devaluation of the Rupee.

The Apex Court therefore held that the notional annual income of the deceased should be considered at a sum of Rs.30,000/- and the multiplier of 15 had to be adopted as provided under the schedule NC:
2023:KHC-K:1365 applicable to a claim under Section 163-A of the M.V.Act, 1988.
He contended that the accident in the case of Kishan Gopal (supra) happened in the year 1992 and the Apex Court assessed the notional annual income of Rs.30,000/- in the year 2014.

He therefore submitted that from the year 2014 till the date of the accident in the present case i.e., in the year 2020, the value of the Rupee has depreciated by nearly 36% at the rate of 6% per year.
He therefore submits that the Tribunal ought to have considered the same while determining notional annual income of the deceased.

The learned counsel relied upon the judgment of this Court in MFA No.201352/2022 and contended that this Court had considered the annual notional income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.45,000/- by considering the rate of inflation at 5%.
He therefore prayed that same principle be applied in the present case also.

8. The learned counsel for the respondent/Corporation submitted that since the deceased NC:
2023:KHC-K:1365 was 6 years old boy, the possibility of child being negligent cannot be ruled out and therefore, the Corporation should not be made responsible for the negligence of the deceased.

He submitted that the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Kishan Gopal (supra) is consistently followed through out the country and notional annual income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.30,000/- considered by the Apex Court is just and proper having regard to the fact that the deceased was not an earning member.
9.
I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellants/claimants as well as learned counsel for the respondent/Corporation.

10. As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the appellants/claimants a claim under Section 166 of the M.V.Act, 1988, should be determined taking into account the value of the rupee as it exists today and that would be the just compensation payable to the claimant.

As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the appellants the NC: 2023:KHC-K:1365 notional annual income determined in the year 2014 cannot be applied for the accident that happened in the year 2020 without factoring the rate of inflation and consequent devaluation of the rupee.

11. In that view of the matter, this Court considers it appropriate to factor the rate of inflation at 5%
per annum from 2014 till 2020.
If the same is done, the notional annual income has to be considered at the rate of Rs.39,000/-.
Since the deceased was a minor aged 6 years, the maximum multiplier of 18 is to be applied.

Hence, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be enhanced to a sum of Rs.7,02,000/- towards loss of dependency and a sum of Rs.88,000/- towards loss of filial consortium and a sum of Rs.33,000/- towards loss of estate, funeral expenses and incidental expenses.

Thus, in all the claimant would be entitled to enhanced compensation of Suvarna And Anr vs The Managing Director on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41370579/

sentences.text:
In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part and the compensation of Rs.5,05,000/-
determined by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.8,23,000/-.

The enhanced compensation of Rs.3,18,000/- shall be paid by the Corporation to the claimants along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.

The enhanced compensation amount along with interest shall be deposited by the Corporation before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment and award.
Upon deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be deposited in the name of claimant No.1 in any nationalized Bank for a period of 3 years.
